To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the follicular fluid (FF) of cows with spontaneous oestrus had the most favourable acid-base parameters, oestradiol and progesterone concentrations, while the FF of cows with follicular cysts had the worst parameters.
the follicular fluids of IO and CYS group had disturbances of intrafolliculintracystic acid-base environment and hormonal profile.

the follicular fluids (pO2 and pCO2) of IO and CYS cows are deviated from physiological values, which can affect the quality of oocytes and granulosa cells, while the steroid concentrations in the FF and plasma of IO and CYST cows are lower than in cows with a normal estrus cycle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the acid-base parameters, steroid levels in the FF and plasma of cows with CYS or SO or IO and their correlations.
the physiological and biochemical changes of follicular fluid and blood of dairy cows with spontaneous oestrus, induced oestrus and follicular cyst.
the acid-base balance, steroid hormones and the oocyte quality in dairy cows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
follicular cysts are a pathological entity and that they should not be confused with pre-ovulatory dominant follicles.
acid-base balance, steroid concentrations in FF and plasma of cows with spontaneous or induced oestruses were more physiological than in animals with follicular cysts.
the follicular cysts and induced oestrus cows are characterized by a disturbance of intrafollicle acid-base balance and by a decrease in steroid concentrations in follicular fluid and plasma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intrafollicular environment of the pre-ovulatory and cystic follicle is different in terms of acid-base and steroid parameters.
the follicular fluid and blood acid-base balance and the steroid levels are different between cows with SO, IO and CYS.
the acid-base parameters, steroid concentrations in the FF and blood and their correlations are different among cows with SO, IO and CYS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
follicular cysts are associated with a disturbed intrafollicular environment.
the acid-base balance of the follicle is an important parameter for the evaluation of the follicle's health status.

the acid-base parameters and steroid concentration profiles of FF in IO and CYP groups were similar to each other, which indicates the similarity of the intrafollicular and intracystic environments in these groups.
